exposure: maternal serum high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels
cohort: The study included 5407 pregnant women without diabetes mellitus, hypertension, thyroid disorders, or fetal malformation, who gave birth to single live babies at term.
finding: Higher maternal serum triglyceride (TG) levels and lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels at late gestation are independently associated with an increased risk of neonatal macrosomia in women without diabetes mellitus.
